note: Held-out descriptions, written 2026-11-08 after the 6A rules were tuned on cases.json. Neither the rules nor the prompt may be changed on the strength of these cases. A case counts only when its label is 'reviewed' by Paige.

cases.text: Our HR assistant answers new hires' questions about benefits and sends each of them a welcome pack on their first day.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: "HR assistant" could be the AI or a person's job title.

cases.text: The AI reads incoming insurance claims, pulls the policy details, and recommends approve, deny or investigate; adjusters make the final call.
cases.label: draft

cases.text: Tenants text the bot about repairs. It logs each request and books a contractor visit for anything marked urgent.
cases.label: draft

cases.text: Teachers paste in student essays and the model suggests feedback comments; nothing is shown to students until the teacher edits and releases it.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Student work may be regulated (education records); asked rather than assumed.

cases.text: When a delivery is late, customers automatically get an apology email and a $5 credit.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Something automated sends and credits; the AI isn't named. Follows the frozen labelling rule "automated isn't AI" (DECISIONS.md, Phase 6B boundaries, 2026-10-22; prompt describe-v1 rule 6).

cases.text: The assistant can look up a caller's last five orders, but it cannot change or cancel anything; refunds are always handled by the billing team.
cases.label: draft

cases.text: Eventually we'd like the model to reorder stock on its own. For now it just flags items that are running low.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: A future wish isn't current behaviour.

cases.text: The pharmacy chatbot answers questions about opening hours and checks whether a prescription is ready.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Prescription status is health information in a regulated setting.

cases.text: Our fraud model scores every card transaction in real time and blocks the ones above 0.9; analysts review the blocks each morning.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Blocking a transaction is acting. Fraud screening may be regulated.

cases.text: It drafts grant applications from our past proposals. It never submits anything, but it does send the finished draft to our director by email.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: "Never submits anything" and sending an internal email are compatible: the negation is scoped to submitting (negation-scope, not a contradiction). Sending the email itself is acting (acts: yes).

cases.text: Site managers upload photos of the scaffolding and the tool lists possible safety hazards for them to check.
cases.label: draft

cases.text: Guests book tables through the website; the AI only answers questions about the menu and allergens.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Guests book, through the website; the AI only answers.

cases.text: Applicants upload their passport and two payslips; the system checks the documents and decides whether the rental application goes forward.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: "The system decides": automated, AI not named; tenant screening may be regulated. Follows the frozen labelling rule "automated isn't AI" (DECISIONS.md, Phase 6B boundaries, 2026-10-22; prompt describe-v1 rule 6).

cases.text: Support tickets are summarised overnight and the summaries are posted to the team's Slack channel each morning.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Posted by something not named (acts: ask); the team receiving the summaries counts as people: yes. Summarising doesn't establish a work type in the list, so "does" isn't scored (Paige, 2026-11-08). Follows the frozen labelling rule "automated isn't AI" (DECISIONS.md, Phase 6B boundaries, 2026-10-22; prompt describe-v1 rule 6).

cases.text: Nothing about patients goes into the tool: it only drafts the clinic's social media posts, which our office manager approves and publishes.
cases.label: draft
cases.note: Clinic setting, but no patient work is described. sensitive: no and regulated: no mean "don't propose these facts from this description"; they are not proof that sensitive data or regulatory obligations are absent. A question is acceptable.
